data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from PBS)

# PBS requested:
#   -l nodes=1:ppn=1:haswell,walltime=24:00:00,mem=8gb
#   -o <Processing Folder>
#   -e <Processing Folder>

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 1 \
  --time=24h \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: PBS mem=8gb has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: PBS node property ":haswell" (CPU model constraint) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: you may run on a different CPU generation, affecting performance and (rarely)
# compatibility if binaries rely on specific instruction sets.

# NOTE: PBS -o/-e point to placeholders (<Processing Folder>), and PBS normally expects file paths.
# There is no concrete path to translate; leaving log handling to default shell behavior.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but logs may not land in the intended directory.

module load singularity-3.2.1

singularity exec -B <directory of run_qunex.sh>,<directory of parameter file>,<directory of gradient_coefficient_files>:/export/HCP/gradient_coefficient_files <path to qunex oontainer/qunex.sif> <directory of run_qunex.sh>/run_qunex.sh \
  --parameterfolder=<directory of parameter file> \
  --studyfolder=<Processing Folder>/<subject_name> \
  --subjects=<subject_name> \
  --scan=<scan_name> \
  --overwrite=yes \
  --hcppipelineprocess=FunctionalPreprocessing
'
"
}
